newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia kangaroo meat exports set to bound.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia kangaroo meat exports set to bound.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday that France's approval last week for the sale of kangaroo meat for human consumption would open a new export market worth up to A$30 million a year for Australian exporters.

The move followed months of negotiations between Australian and French officials as Australia sought to expand its A$3 million-a-year European market, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson and Trade Minister Tim Fischer said in a statement.

"Australia was able to present France with extensive scientific and technical information about kangaroo meat and the high standards of game processing plants in this country, enabling them to arrive at this decision," Anderson said.
Fischer said the French decision brought France into line with several other European countries, including Germany and Britain, which had long allowed imports of kangaroo meat for human consumption.
Europe is Australia's major market for game meat exports.
Anderson said the French move would boost Australia's kangaroo meat industry. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
